name: Vieille maîtresse
notes: Sector that stays sunny for a long time despite the trees.
Rock of variable quality, but decent overall.
routes: La cheminée de l'enfant de chœur
Easy route in a wide chimney (old descent route); chimneying technique may come in handy. Unstable blocks — be vigilant.
Surprising, mixed route. Steps, then a nice slab.
Slightly polished classic. Two technical moves in a corner. Fun overall.
Starting variant of 178. Athletic in a wide crack. Intense start.
Sustained, vertical climbing. Nice, really physical route on good holds.
Varied route. Slightly nasty start, rock with loose flakes after that, and a nice slab of sloping pockets to finish. Mixed, but very fun all the same.
Consistent, technical finger climbing. A must-do.
The Man Who Walked Through Walls
Major route at the grade. Intense start on edges and water drips, followed by a crack in very sculpted rock. Fairly pumpy overall.
Intense start on an overhanging pillar that needs careful reading beforehand. The second part is less intense but technically demanding.
Mixed route. A series of small slabs with technical problems, broken up by good rests.
Consistent but not very sustained. Rather balance-oriented in the first part, followed by a traverse right at the niche on good edges. Fun.
Finishing variant of 186. Straight up above the niche. Fingery.
Consistent, technical slab climbing. Nice big moves. Tends to be run-out.
Finishing variant of 188. Nicely consistent. Steep, technical slab.
Bouldery. Slab with spaced holds at the start, then a rest, then a thin flake and a demanding compact slab.
Traversing route with an original path. Committing and unusual. Not the most interesting at the grade.
Consistent, sustained and demanding route. Crimps on a slab to tame. There is a bees' nest at the time of writing.
Finishing variant of 192. A demanding boulder move to leave the niche.
